entities.name: Peer review attitudes
observations: In a single-academic-hospital survey (36 respondents), 86% considered peer review important for patient care and 81% for professional development; 92% preferred anonymity (PMID:25439617).
Concerns included malpractice safety (72%), workplace relationships (67%), and job security or rankings (42%) (PMID:25439617).

source_tools.relevance: Survey of radiologist attitudes to departmental peer review

entities.name: Peer review utility concerns
observations: Among 50 faculty respondents, 44% called the existing system a waste of time and 58% saw it as regulatory compliance; 46% perceived performance improvement and 32% error reduction (PMID:24144835).

entities.name: Peer learning preferences
observations: In a pediatric radiologist survey (219 responses), 86% rated comment-enhanced feedback important for performance improvement versus 48% for numerical scores; 82% said comments were more effective, and 93% thought peer-learning conferences could benefit practice (PMID:30923884).
At one tertiary center, 70.4% of 27 radiologists preferred peer learning over score-based peer review after transition (PMID:38113549).

source_tools.relevance: Survey and local transition evidence for peer-learning preference

entities.name: Peer learning adoption
observations: In an ACR member survey, 53% of 1,153 respondents reported using peer learning; response rate was 6%, limiting representativeness (PMID:37230234).
An abdominal division pilot found all survey respondents considered a no-blame culture important and 70% favored anonymous case presentations (PMID:39890515).
